newsitem.title: USA: Weapon scare forces evacuation at Calif. airport.
newsitem.headline: Weapon scare forces evacuation at Calif. airport.

text.p: A weapon scare forced the evacuation of up to 2,000 travelers on Monday at San Jose International Airport, delaying 10 flights for more than an hour, airport officials said.

Terminal A, the busiest at the airport, was evacuated after a bag containing what appeared to be a gun got through a security checkpoint, spokeswoman Cathy Gaskell said. Airport officials said the bag was seen going through an X-ray machine but disappeared before officials could ask any questions.

About 10 flights at the San Jose airport, 40 miles (64 km) south of San Francisco, were delayed for about 90 minutes as airport security searched for the weapon and the person carrying it. "We're still searching," Gaskell said.
Although the weapon has yet to be found, she said, airport officials were now allowing travelers to re-enter the terminal and flights to resume.
